newsitem.title: USA: Northwest delays Washington gas line outage.
newsitem.headline: Northwest delays Washington gas line outage.

text.p: Northwest Pipeline said Wednesday a scheduled outage to replace a damaged crankshaft at its Chehalis gas compressor station in Washington has been delayed due to problems with the replacement crankshaft.

"We had a problem yesterday. That's going to set back the in-service date by three days," said company spokeswoman Susan Hartje, noting the new in-service date, or the date by which the station would be fully restored, would be November 4.
The partial outage, which began October 1, has affected about 150-190 million cubic feet per day of gas, or about 25 percent of primary capacity at the Chehalis pumping station.
Problems occurred Tuesday when plant operators were unable to fit the replacement crankshaft, taken from the Sumner pumping station, she said.
Sumner was already scheduled to be shut for its annual maintenance through the end of the year.
Northwest is a unit of the Williams Companies Inc.
